dataSources: `sourcetype=fgt_event` subtype=system, logid related to admin/config Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
spl:
index=sase sourcetype="fgt_event" subtype="system" earliest=-30d
| where match(lower(msg),"(?i)config|policy|rule|admin.*login|object.*modified")
| stats count earliest(_time) as first latest(_time) as last values(msg) as actions by user, ui
| sort -last
description: FortiSASE policies are centrally managed and affect all connected users globally. Configuration audit logs enable change tracking, compliance, and root-cause analysis when policies cause access issues.
value: Security governance teams audit all FortiSASE administrative configuration changes, flagging security profile deletions, out-of-hours modifications, and high-impact changes to firewall policies, ZTNA rules, and web filter profiles that could create immediate security gaps.
implementation: Forward FortiSASE management audit events. Alert on after-hours changes or bulk policy modifications. Correlate with ITSM change tickets.
visualization: Table (admin changes), Timeline (configuration events), Bar chart (changes by admin).

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• FortiSASE admin audit events in `index=fortisase` with `sourcetype=fortisase:event` or `sourcetype=fortisase:audit`. Key fields: `user` (admin), `action` (login/logout/add/edit/delete), `msg` (description), `cfgpath` (configuration path changed), `cfgobj` (object name), `devname`.
• FortiSASE configuration changes can have immediate impact: modifying a security profile, changing ZTNA rules, or altering SD-WAN policies affect all connected users and sites.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Verify admin audit events:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype IN ("fortisase:event","fortisase:audit") earliest=-30d
| where isnotnull(cfgpath) OR match(action, "(?i)add|edit|delete")
| stats count by action, cfgpath
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Primary search — Configuration change audit:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype IN ("fortisase:event","fortisase:audit") earliest=-7d
| where isnotnull(cfgpath) OR match(action, "(?i)add|edit|delete")
| eval change_hour=strftime(_time, "%H")
| eval out_of_hours=if(change_hour<"08" OR change_hour>"18", "YES", "no")
| table _time, user, action, cfgpath, cfgobj, msg, out_of_hours
| sort - _time
```

Understanding this SPL: Lists all FortiSASE configuration changes with timing. Changes to `firewall/policy`, `webfilter/profile`, `ips/sensor`, or `ztna/rule` are high-impact. Out-of-hours changes are flagged. A deleted security profile may leave policies without protection.

High-impact changes:
```spl
index=fortisase sourcetype IN ("fortisase:event","fortisase:audit") earliest=-7d
| where match(cfgpath, "(?i)policy|profile|sensor|ztna|security") OR action="delete"
| stats count by user, action, cfgpath
| sort - count
```

Step 3 — Validate
(a) Make a test config change. Verify audit event.
(b) In FortiSASE: Log & Report > Event Log > System Events.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard: Row 1 — Changes per day. Row 2 — High-impact changes. Row 3 — Out-of-hours.
Alert: Immediate on security profile deletion.

Runbook:
1. **Profile deleted** — May break dependent policies. Verify and restore.
2. **Out-of-hours change** — Verify with admin. Document justification.
3. **Many changes by one admin** — Could be automation or a bulk mistake.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **No audit events** — Event logging may be filtered. Check FortiSASE log settings.
• **`cfgpath` empty** — Login/logout events don't include config paths. Filter for config changes only.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`TA-fortinet_fortigate` (FortiSASE admin audit) — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=fgt_event into sase. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`ui, user`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Every time an administrator changes our FortiSASE security settings, we record it. We especially watch for deletions of security rules and changes made at unusual hours, because a single wrong change to our cloud security system can affect every employee at once.
